assets.prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Create one sober engineering concept visualization for an early electrical and thermal laboratory test fixture. Landscape 3:2 on clean off-white background, precise studio 3D illustration with restrained slate blue PCB, aluminium carrier, natural copper, no dramatic glowing effects. Show an open small bench enclosure in three-quarter view. It contains a cool control and measurement PCB on the left and a physically separate removable thermal test coupon on a metal heat spreader on the right, connected by short labelled power and sensor cables. Four modest chassis-mounted resistive heater loads are on the thermal carrier, five small temperature sensing locations and a four-wire RTD lead. Keep heater power wiring distinct from measurement leads. Low voltage external bench supply connector, USB data connector, a hardwired abort connector and a simple physical enable switch, without implying a completed design. Do NOT include a quantum chip in this fixture, no monolithic custom ASIC. Show an optional standard FPGA mezzanine as a small unpopulated expansion connector on the cool board, not an installed processor. No RF hardware in this base illustration. Draw only a few functional components with plausible engineering appearance, no fake exact net routing or certification markings. Large exact heading 'ACVM ETF-01'. Second line 'Electrical & Thermal Test Fixture'. Three short callout labels only: 'CONTROL BOARD', 'THERMAL COUPON', 'EXTERNAL DC'. Clear footer exact 'KONZEPT 0.1  |  NICHT MASSSTAEBLICH  |  NICHT GEFERTIGT'. Every word legible, no additional invented technical specifications, no dimensions, no performance numbers, no PASS indicators, no manufactured-device or safety-certification claims. This image communicates spatial intent only.

Use case: scientific-educational concept illustration. Create one standalone sober engineering visualization of a possible future quantum dot test chip, NOT a proven quantum processor or fabrication drawing. Landscape 3:2, white background, scientific publication clarity, restrained gold and slate blue with pale grey layered material. Exact main title 'ASTROLABIUM QD-01'. Subtitle 'Quantum Dot Test Device'. A large overview on the left shows an illustrative square research die on an open ceramic laboratory carrier with bond pads and a small central device region; keep die proportions generic without dimensions. On the right show a magnified conceptual device region with ONE gate-defined target quantum dot and ONE adjacent charge-sensing quantum dot in separate parallel conduction channels, reservoirs at channel ends, split/barrier/plunger gates above an encapsulated sheet. Use simple electrostatic gate geometry, not a triangle, not a Kagome lattice, not a seven-metal CMOS chip. Below the magnified region, a small exploded materials illustration shows, top to bottom, illustrative metal gate layers with an intervening dielectric, upper hBN, AB-stacked bilayer graphene, lower hBN, graphite local back gate, insulating support. Make no atomic-resolution or exact-thickness claim. Labels limited to 'TEST DOT', 'CHARGE SENSOR', 'DC GATES', 'RF SENSE', and 'BLG VARIANTE'. All views must visibly be conceptual drawings; no SEM texture masquerading as measured microscopy. Clear footer exact 'FORSCHUNGSENTWURF 0.1  |  NICHT MASSSTAEBLICH  |  KEINE FERTIGUNGSFREIGABE'. Do not add numeric scales, nanometre dimensions, timing, fidelity, quantum state vectors, performance scores, certifications, production readiness, QND claims, or X/Y valley-control claims. This is an illustrative material candidate whose fabrication and quantum control remain to be established.
